questions.title: Consequence of FDA pregnancy category D
questions.question: A drug has been classified under "D" in FDA pregnancy categories. What would be the consequences of using that drug?

options.A: Animal studies have demonstrated adverse effects
options.B: Fetal risk has been demonstrated, in certain circumstances benefits could outweighs the risk
options.D: Fetal risk has been demonstrated, the risk outweighs any possible benefit to the mother

explanations.A: Incorrect. Adverse effects only in animal studies, with no human data, describes category C, a less certain level of risk than category D, which is based on demonstrated risk from human data or experience, not animal studies alone.
explanations.B: Correct. Category D means fetal risk has been demonstrated, from animal studies, human studies, or post-marketing experience. The drug may still be justified in certain circumstances, typically a serious maternal illness with no safer alternative, because its potential benefit could outweigh that known risk.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "No risk to the fetus" would describe category A, the safest category, not category D, which specifically means risk has been demonstrated.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Risk always outweighs benefit" describes category X, an absolute contraindication -- category D instead leaves room for the drug to be used if the benefit outweighs the risk in a given case.

questions.learning_objective: State the prescribing consequence of FDA pregnancy category D: demonstrated risk, but usable if benefit outweighs that risk.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Fetal risk has been demonstrated, in certain circumstances benefits could outweighs the risk."

questions.title: Consequence of FDA pregnancy category X
questions.question: A drug has been classified under "X" in FDA pregnancy categories. What would be the consequences of using that drug?

options.A: Fetal risk has been demonstrated, in certain circumstances benefits could outweighs the risk
options.C: Animal studies have demonstrated no adverse effects
options.D: Fetal risk has been demonstrated, the risk outweighs any possible benefit to the mother

explanations.A: Incorrect. "Benefits could outweigh the risk in certain circumstances" describes category D, not category X -- category X instead means the risk always outweighs any possible benefit, with no justified-use exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. "No risk to the fetus" would describe category A, the safest category, the opposite of category X, which carries demonstrated risk that outweighs any benefit.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "No adverse effects in animal studies" would describe category A or B, not category X, which is defined by demonstrated fetal risk, not an absence of it.
explanations.D: Correct. Category X means fetal risk has been demonstrated, and that risk outweighs any possible benefit to the mother under any circumstance. Category X drugs are therefore contraindicated in pregnancy, with no risk-benefit exception the way category D allows.

questions.learning_objective: State the prescribing consequence of FDA pregnancy category X: demonstrated risk that always outweighs benefit, an absolute contraindication.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Fetal risk has been demonstrated, the risk outweighs any possible benefit to the mother."
